result.title: From Human Corrections to Learned Segmentations: A Critical Mathematical Review of Information, Learning, and Human Effort
result.comment: 40 pages, literature-selection and search record included
result.summary: When does a human correction become useful learning, and what establishes better segmentation at matched human effort? This critical narrative review follows feedback through its selection, learner update, and evaluation. It compares active learning, machine teaching, interactive segmentation, and sequential predictive evaluation using a common mathematical account of target information, predictive error, response predictability, and human work. An exact Bayesian update converts evaluation-label information into expected log-loss improvement; an excess-risk decomposition explains what an approximate learner can lose. Conditional information decompositions separate the roles of selected locations, labels, and displayed context. Empirical comparisons show why response protocols, update mechanisms, and effort denominators matter, distinguishing current-mask refinement from reusable learning and simulated interaction from human evidence. We identify what logs can reveal, what requires independent evaluation, and what remains model-dependent. The resulting research priorities are to test what selection reveals, whether using it improves assimilation, and whether the resulting interaction policy benefits segmentation at matched effort. These are distinct claims: predicting a teacher's responses need not identify human intentions or establish better learning. No new acquisition algorithm or empirical superiority is claimed.

AI.brief_summary: 这是一篇约 40 页的批判性综述，用统一的信息论与风险评估框架比较主动学习、机器教学、交互式分割与顺序预测评估，试图回答人类纠正何时转化为有效学习、以及在同等人工投入下如何定义「更好的分割」，本身不提出新的采集算法或声称性能更优。
AI.relevance_reason: 其条件信息分解、超额风险分解与「同等投入」评价口径，可能为 LVR 中视觉证据筛选的实际贡献、选中位置与标签的相对信息量、以及 latent 步骤是否真正被后续推理使用提供可核查的分析视角；但领域为分割与人机交互，暂无与 VLM 推理的直接联系。
